subject: POC capacity: deployment choice & GPU mix (follow-up)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Quick follow-up + ask: deployment mode & token mix for POC

Hi Emily / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great discussion. Per our call I wanted to summarize the open items we need from your side to finalize a tight Dedicated capacity proposal and deployment recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC). If you can confirm the items below it will let us size the pool and give you concrete cost / SLA options for the POC.

1) Peak TPS target (in requests/sec) and expected 95th/99th latency SLOs
2) Typical prompt/response token mix (avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens) — if you can share a sample CSV that’s perfect
3) Preferred deployment mode for the POC: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved pool, or Private VPC (customer-managed network)
4) Any hard security reqs (e.g., IP allowlist, customer KMS, SOC2 evidence needed for procurement)

Initial notes from our side: for NLG-heavy flows with 200–500 TPS we recommend H100 80GB or a mix of A100/ H100 depending on the model quantization and latency targets; for <50 TPS A10G / A100 40GB may be more cost-effective. We’ll prepare two sizing options once we have the numbers above.

I attached a small token-profile CSV template you can drop your samples into (olive_token_profile_v1.csv).

Next steps: if you can reply with the TPS and token profile by EOD Thursday I’ll push a proposal and a POC timeline.

Thanks — Rafael

--

Rafael —

Thanks for the recap. Attached a quick token sample exported from our staging traffic and a short notes column (olive_token_profile_v1.csv). Highlights:
- Peak observed (staging burst): ~120 TPS for the one endpoint we demoed
- Steady-state expected for POC: 40–60 TPS
- Prompt tokens: avg 68; completion tokens: avg 420 (we use longer completions for summaries)
- 80% of calls are single-turn, 20% are multi-turn chat (KV cache advisable)

On deployment preference: we prefer Dedicated reserved pool for the POC — we want predictable throughput and data isolation but don’t require an on-prem VPC yet. Procurement is also more straightforward for a reserved contract.

Security: We will need customer-managed KMS and a SOC2 attestation for procurement.

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if helpful.

Emily

emily.santos@olivetech.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + ask: deployment mode & token mix for POC

Great — thanks for the details, Emily. Based on the numbers you provided here are two concrete Dedicated pool options for the POC (30-day window):

Option A — Cost-optimized (steady 50 TPS, occasional bursts to 120 TPS)
- GPU mix: 4x A100 40GB (shared across instances using continuous batching)
- Estimated concurrency: 16 concurrent requests per GPU with batching (depends on model bertched profile)
- Expected 95% latency: 120–220 ms; 99% ~ 400–600 ms for 420-token completions
- Notes: lower cost, good for quantized 4-bit opt models; supports prefix caching for multi-turn to reduce cost

Option B — Latency-first (smoother 99th latency for long completions)
- GPU mix: 2x H100 80GB + 2x A100 40GB (heterogeneous pool)
- Estimated concurrency: 24 concurrent requests per H100 for shorter sequences, and 12 on A100 for heavy completions
- Expected 95% latency: 90–170 ms; 99% ~ 250–380 ms for 420-token completions
- Notes: higher cost but improves tail latency and supports larger KV cache per device

Security/Compliance: We can enable customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and provide SOC2 Type II report and audit logs for procurement. For Private VPC we’d need network peering and an install window; since you prefer Dedicated now we’ll keep that in reserve.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short POC SOW sketch + pricing (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf) — this is preliminary and will be refined after you pick Option A or B and confirm the target TPS / P95 latency.

Next steps I propose:
- Emily: confirm Option A or B (or tell us an acceptable budget / latency tradeoff)
- Marissa: I asked her to draft a 30-day POC SOW and a rack-level ops runbook for the pool
- Karthik: internal sizing validation / any kernel/quantization constraints to call out

If helpful I can also run a small internal microbenchmark matching your token distribution once you confirm.

Thanks — Rafael
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Emily Santos <emily.santos@olivetech.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + ask: deployment mode & GPU mix for POC

Emily / Rafael — quick technical note to help inform the choice:

- Given avg completion length ~420 tokens we should prioritize device memory for KV cache. H100 80GB gives ~2–3x KV capacity vs A100 40GB which matters for multi-turn latency.
- If Olive will use mixed-precision quantized models (4-bit), throughput on A100 is reasonable; H100 benefits more for larger context windows and reduced kernel overhead on long sequences.
- For Option A we’d add a small caching layer (prefix cache at the model invocation layer) to cut costs on 80% single-turn calls. That typically reduces token compute by ~18–25% observed in similar POCs.
- We can start the POC with Option A and a staged upgrade path: switch two A100s -> H100s if tail latency needs tighten after initial telemetry.

I’ll prep the benchmarking commands and link to the kernel perf notes in the shared Drive folder.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
